_source: Visibility requirements for hidden employee profiles. Items still to be decided are shown without an answer rather than assumed.

principle.text: RM, HR, Admin or a similar privileged role can always see and search a hidden profile. Everyone else is governed by the rule on each screen below.

rules.name: Listed and marked
rules.text: The person appears for anyone who can open the screen, carrying the hidden-profile treatment (tinted row + icon).

rules.name: Privileged viewers only
rules.text: The row exists only for the named roles. For everyone else it is absent — not greyed out, not disabled. Absent.

rules.name: Not listed for anyone
rules.text: Excluded from the list, dropdown or result set for every viewer, privileged roles included.

rules.name: Reporting manager only
rules.text: Visible to the reporting manager alone — narrower than V2, which also includes HR and Admin.

rules.name: Not decided
rules.text: This item is flagged as an open question in the requirements. No rule has been chosen; developers must not assume one.

rows.not: Every other role — the person returns no result
rows.flag: The hidden person does not appear in search results for non-privileged roles. They can still use search themselves — this is a visibility rule, not an access-control restriction.
rows.verified_note: NOT A ROUTE — header control; no path in the app's route table. Correct, but it means there is no screen to point a developer at.

rows.sees: Everyone with access to the People employee list
rows.treatment: Tinted row + incognito icon; hidden by default behind the Hidden filter

rows.verified_note: sub-sidebar flyout — nav label is 'Exit Management', but the ROUTE is /separation

rows.flag: The original requirement bundled four screens (Profile Update Requests, Employment Changes, PIP, Probation Management) into one row. They are separate screens and are split here for clarity.

rows.verified_note: sub-sidebar flyout — the app calls it 'PIP Management'
sub-sidebar flyout — note the route lands on the 'active-probation' tab

rows.flag: This is the only screen where the requirement explicitly names the RM alone and excludes HR/Admin. Confirm whether that is deliberate or whether the global principle (RM + HR + Admin always see) overrides it.
rows.verified_note: route_table — My Team has TWO screens: /my-team/employee-listing and /my-team/job-interviews

rows.sees: RM and higher admin / HR roles
rows.flag: The requirement says "if possible". Removing a node from a hierarchy creates a structural problem — if the hidden person has direct reports, their subtree becomes orphaned. The chart's behaviour in that case is NOT DECIDED and needs a product decision before implementation.

The requirement is the question itself: "Should a restricted person be able to book meeting rooms — yes or no?" This is unanswered. Note: this is about what the person can DO (access control), not who can see them (visibility). The only item in this list of that kind.
rows.verified_note: route_table — the app calls it 'Meeting Rooms'

rows.flag: This screen shows counts and charts, not a list of people. There is no row to hide: a hidden profile is counted in every total and every chart segment unless the underlying figures exclude them. Whether they should is still to be decided.

rows.verified_note: route_table — the route and label are PLURAL

rows.treatment: Highlighted row + "Includes N hidden profiles" on the count
rows.flag: Dev note: The requirement specified "Highlight Restricted row" only for Employees Compensation and Tax Declaration. Screens 3–6 were listed without specifying a treatment. The same highlight treatment has been applied to all six for consistency — this is inferred, not explicitly stated in the requirements.
rows.verified_note: route_table + captured DOM (this is the screen already built)
route_table — the app calls it 'Expense Management'

rows.flag: This screen shows counts and charts, not a list of people. There is no row to hide: a hidden profile is counted in every total and every chart segment unless the underlying figures exclude them. Whether they should is still to be decided.

rows.treatment: Absent from the selectable panellist list
rows.flag: This is an ELIGIBILITY rule, not just a visibility one — the person cannot be chosen as a panellist at all. Edge case: if an existing panellist is later marked hidden, the behaviour for their already-scheduled interviews is not specified.
rows.verified_note: captured DOM — the real control is a field labelled 'Interview Panel' (tooltip: 'Select members responsible for this interview'), and a column of the same name. There is no 'panellist' anywhere in the app.

rows.treatment: Name not shown to the external viewer
rows.verified_note: No screen of this name was identified in the application. The screen needs confirming before this rule can be built.

rows.flag: This form selects an employee from the shared employee list. Whether a hidden profile can be selected here is still to be decided.

This form selects an employee from the shared employee list. Whether a hidden profile can be selected here is still to be decided.

This screen shows counts and charts, not a list of people. There is no row to hide: a hidden profile is counted in every total and every chart segment unless the underlying figures exclude them. Whether they should is still to be decided.

The requirement reads "if the person is/has the restricted employee under the team/organization" and stops mid-sentence. It's listed under "Will Come" (meaning visible), but never specifies to whom. Cannot be implemented from this — needs a product clarification.

rows.screen: Contacts, Companies, Leads, Deals, Client Interviews, Invoices, Payments
rows.treatment: Records created by the person are filtered out
rows.flag: This filters RECORDS BY THEIR CREATOR, not employee rows. It's a fundamentally different mechanism from every other row in this map and touches seven record types. Likely the largest engineering effort in this list.
rows.verified_note: route_table — 7 record types, each its own listing

rows.screen: Contacts / Deals / Leads / Client Interviews — Add
rows.flag: These four Add forms select an employee in order to ASSIGN a record to them. That is the reverse of the rule above, which covers records the person CREATED. The two are separate rules and each needs its own decision.
This screen selects an employee from the shared employee list. Whether a hidden profile can be selected here is still to be decided.

This screen shows counts and charts, not a list of people. There is no row to hide: a hidden profile is counted in every total and every chart segment unless the underlying figures exclude them. Whether they should is still to be decided.

Open decision tree: (1) Should the person be allowed into a project as a resource? (2) If YES — should tickets assigned to them be visible to everyone? (3) If NO — they cannot be added as a resource at all. Answer (1) first; it determines whether (2) is relevant.

The requirement says "only the reporting manager will decide the same" — the word is 'decide', not 'see'. This may mean the RM controls allocation decisions rather than being the only viewer. Interpreted here as RM-only visibility — needs confirmation.
rows.verified_note: route_table — these are TWO separate screens: /daily-allocation and /resource-planner
